title: Webhook signatures
description: Verify signed monitoring webhooks from DID.is with the SDK helpers, and handle retries safely.
---

import { Tabs, TabItem } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import CaseDiagram from '../../../components/CaseDiagram.astro';

When you monitor identifiers in the [console](/app/monitoring/), DID.is sends an HTTPS request to your endpoint when something changes, for example a DID document or its domain binding. Each request is signed with your webhook secret, so your receiver can tell it really came from DID.is for your project.

Here **your receiver does the checking**, not DID.is. Verify every request before you act on it. The SDK helpers do this in one call.

<CaseDiagram

  returns="verified event"

  result={{ tone: 'info', text: 'act, or answer 401' }}
/>

## What a valid signature shows

- **Origin.** The body was signed with your project's webhook secret, so it came from DID.is (or from someone who has your secret).
- **Integrity.** The body was not changed in transit.
- **Scope.** The event belongs to the tenant and project you expect.

## What it does not show

- **Anything more about the identifier** than the event itself says. A `document.changed` event says the document changed, not whether the change is legitimate.
- **That the event is new.** Retries resend the same event. You must remove duplicates yourself.
- **A paid entitlement.** A valid signature is not a billing grant.

## Headers

| Header | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `X-DIDIS-Event-ID` | The event ID, `cevent_…`. Same on every retry. |
| `X-DIDIS-Signature` | `t=<createdAt>,v1=<hex HMAC-SHA256>` |

The signed bytes are `<t>.<raw body>`: the timestamp, a period, then the exact request body. Verify against the raw body before parsing it; re-serialized JSON will not match.

## Verify with the SDK

The helpers check the HMAC-SHA256 signature, the timestamp (not more than 60 seconds in the future, not older than 30 days by default), `specVersion` (`didis.customer-monitor.v1`), that the event's `createdAt` equals the signed timestamp, and that the event's `id`, `tenantId` and `projectId` match what you expect. They return `true` or `false`.

<Tabs syncKey="lang">
<TabItem label="TypeScript">
```ts
import { verifyCustomerMonitorSignature } from "@didis/client";

// Express example: use the raw body.
app.post("/didis/webhook", express.text({ type: "*/*" }), async (req, res) => {
  const ok = await verifyCustomerMonitorSignature(
    process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET!,
    req.body, // raw string
    req.get("X-DIDIS-Signature") ?? "",
    {
      tenantId: process.env.TENANT_ID!,
      projectId: process.env.PROJECT_ID!,
      eventId: req.get("X-DIDIS-Event-ID") ?? "",
    },
  );
  if (!ok) return res.sendStatus(401);

  const event = JSON.parse(req.body);
  if (await alreadyProcessed(event.id)) return res.sendStatus(200);
  await recordAndHandle(event);
  res.sendStatus(200);
});
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Python">
```python
from didis import verify_customer_monitor_signature

ok = verify_customer_monitor_signature(
    secret,
    raw_body,  # bytes
    headers["X-DIDIS-Signature"],
    tenant_id=tenant_id,
    project_id=project_id,
    event_id=headers["X-DIDIS-Event-ID"],
)
if not ok:
    return 401
```
</TabItem>
<TabItem label="Shell">
```bash
# Compute the expected v1 value for a saved body, to compare by hand.
T=1791678083   # the t= value from X-DIDIS-Signature
printf '%s.%s' "$T" "$(cat body.json)" \
  | openssl dgst -sha256 -hmac "$WEBHOOK_SECRET" -hex
```
</TabItem>
</Tabs>

Both helpers take an optional maximum age in seconds (`maxAgeSeconds` / `max_age_seconds`), from 1 second up to the 30-day default. Your tenant and project IDs are shown in the console. Keep the secret server-side.

The shell example is for debugging only. `$(cat …)` drops a trailing newline, so it matches only bodies without one; in code, always use the exact raw bytes.

## Reading the result

| Situation | What it means | What to do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Helper returns `true`, event ID is new | A genuine event for your project. | Record the event ID, then act, then answer 2xx. |
| Helper returns `true`, event ID seen before | A retry of an event you already have. | Answer 2xx and do nothing else. |
| Helper returns `false` | Wrong secret, changed body, too old, or not your tenant or project. | Answer 401 and ignore the body. |

## Retries and duplicates

- A delivery fails if your endpoint does not answer 2xx within 10 seconds. DID.is retries up to five attempts in total, after 1, 2, 4 and 8 minutes.
- Retries send the identical event with the same ID and signature timestamp.
- Record the event ID before side effects, and answer duplicates with 2xx.
- Receivers must use HTTPS on port 443 at a public address. Redirects are not followed; a 3xx answer counts as a failure.
